Ribbon-cutting ceremony Credit: Hyundai Glovis
By Alison Koo
27 November 2026
Hyundai Motor’s logistics arm, Hyundai Glovis, has unveiled plans to broaden its third-party customer base as it goes all out to expand into air freight.
At the opening of its dedicated logistics centre in Incheon International Airport on Tuesday, Glovis said it saw opportunities from rising ecommerce volumes and demand for high value-added cargo transport.
Primarily an operator of car-carrier vessels, Glovis is expanding its third-party customer base through its air freight business. It transports APR’s cosmetics and SM Entertainment’s albums to North America and Europe, and provides air express services to Japan for major South Korean beauty brands.
A spokesperson said: “Our vision is to expand services that integrate land, sea, and air transportation, tailored to the specific characteristics and transportation objectives of customers’ cargo.”
Global air cargo demand rose 3.4% year on year in 2025 to a record high, according to IATA. The AI boom this year is expected to add to the growth, with more demand to transport servers and microchips.
Construction of a five-storey, 44,420 sq metre logistics facility – around 3km from the Incheon Airport Cargo Terminal – began in 2023, and by 2 November, Glovis had announced it had received Customs approval to handle express imports.
The first floor handles imports and can process over a million shipments a month. Four high-speed X-ray machines inspect 5,000 shipments an hour and transmit scanned information to Incheon Airport Customs in real time.
The third and fourth levels are responsible for export logistics for cross-border ecommerce sales to overseas consumers, mainly cosmetics, health supplements, and entertainment-related products. It sorts cargo by country, region, and delivery company using 20 sorting conveyors.
Glovis plans to expand the scope of its logistics services by adding the warehousing, sorting, and packing capabilities to its air forwarding expertise.
